source: The image before Plan B, `stt-before`: feat/one-process 246033e (Next 16.3.8 on Node 22.23.3, uvicorn, supervisord), measured in B0.1 on 2026-10-02 (macOS arm64, OrbStack, Docker 29.4.0, linux/arm64). The numbers, the commands and the setup are in the comment on bead stt-plan-b-one-process-runtime-bbs.4. checks.py reads this file for check 14 (and prints the upload baselines beside check 9); change it only by measuring `stt-before` again.

start_seconds.note: docker's start interval during the health check's start period is 5 s, so `healthy` is quantised

idle_rss_mb.note: median of three fresh containers, 40 s after start; frontend is next-server, backend is uvicorn

loaded_rss_mb.note: after /flows was loaded 20 times in a signed-in Chromium, networkidle each

polling.note: 10 signed-in browsers on /flows/<flow>?run=<a run that never ends>, a 60 s window; CPU is a share of one core

pages.note: docs/plans/page-cost.cjs, signed in (auth-preload.cjs), median of three runs; KB are compressed bytes with headers. LCP and TBT move with the machine's load: compare them against a run of stt-before made in the same session, not against these. The sizes and request counts do not move.

uploads.note: Next's growth in resident memory, in MB, by case (the backend behind it grew 0 to 2 MB in every case); a fresh container per case; MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES 3 GiB. Next held the memory 8 s after.
uploads.over_2GiB: the client sends everything and gets no answer (no 413); Next +2111 MB; with Next alone the upstream got 2147418341 of 2200000212 bytes
